  4395	
  4396	Wave L8, item c1, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SpaceTimePositivity.lean`.
  4397	It proves, with nothing supplied, the space-time facts that the deterministic
  4398	proof of the boundedness claim of `P:variational-positive-scores` needs, and
  4399	states narrower forms of two lemmas. TeX at `a284420`:
  4400	`notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex` (standing assumptions lines 4-21,
  4401	`E:raw-occupation-definitions` lines 10-18, `L:occupation-raw-square`
  4402	statement lines 23-42 with `E:occupation-raw-identities` lines 33-37 and the
  4403	bound of line 40, proof lines 44-90) and
  4404	`notes/integrated_intrinsic_constant.tex` (`L:positive-raw-embedding`
  4405	statement lines 22-39 with `E:positive-bochner-inclusion` lines 26-30 and
  4406	`E:positive-raw-mean` lines 33-36; `E:positive-local-spatial-bound` lines
  4407	70-73). The cost `v_Psi`, the mean `h_(Psi,s)` and the class `C_pos` are
  4408	reused from `VariationalDilation` (`rawCost`, `mean`, `CPos`: integral forms of
  4409	`E:compact-raw-cost` and `E:compact-raw-mean`). The physical pairing
  4410	`B_Gamma(F,G) = int (int F(x) G(x-y) dx) Gamma(dy)` is
  4411	`SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair`. New objects: `stPair` (the pairing of the
  4412	time slices `Phi1(s,.)`, `Phi2(t,.)`) and the space-time form
  4413	`stForm a Gamma Phi1 Phi2 = int_(0,1)^2 |s-t|^(-a) B_Gamma(Phi1(s,.), Phi2(t,.))`,
  4414	a Bochner integral for the product Lebesgue measure on `(0,1)^2`. It is the
  4415	integral of `E:positive-bochner-inclusion` with `G = H_sp` written through
  4416	the physical pairing, and `A(g)` of `E:raw-occupation-definitions` at
  4417	`Phi1 = Phi2 = g^2`. `stFormIter` is the same form as an iterated integral,
  4418	verbatim `OccupationCeilingFinite.stForm`, and `stFormIter_eq` identifies the
  4419	two for continuous compactly supported fields. Every field in the principal
  4420	statements (positivity, Cauchy-Schwarz, and the mean and variance identities)
  4421	is a continuous compactly supported real function on `R x R^d`; the TeX's
  4422	fields live in `L^2(I; H_sp)`. Some auxiliary bounds take more general fields
  4423	(for instance `abs_cross_le` only support and pointwise bounds,
  4424	`conv_stronglyMeasurable` only continuity); their rows state them, and some
  4425	of them are totalized (they also hold for Lean's value `0`). Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `a < 1` for
  4426	integrability, `0 < a` for positivity (the mixture representation of the
  4427	kernel needs it), local finiteness of `Gamma` in place of the physical
  4428	covariance bound `E:positive-local-spatial-bound`, evenness of `Gamma` for
  4429	symmetry. Integrability of every integrand of the principal statements is a
  4430	conclusion (`stIntegrand_integrable` and the first two conjuncts of the mean
  4431	identities), so none of them holds through Lean's value `0` of a
  4432	non-integrable Bochner integral; the exceptions are the explicitly totalized
  4433	auxiliary bounds noted in their rows. Proof route (the TeX works in the completed
  4434	Hilbert spaces `H_sp` and `H_t (x) H_sp`): spatial positivity
  4435	`B_Gamma(Q,Q) >= 0` for continuous compactly supported `Q` by uniform
  4436	approximation with mollified test functions; positivity of `stForm` by writing
  4437	`|s-t|^(-a)` as a positive mixture of rank-one kernels
  4438	(`TimeCompletion.kern_eq_mixture`) and Fubini (`weighted_stPair`);
  4439	Cauchy-Schwarz by the discriminant; the identities by Fubini
  4440	(`spatialPair_eq_conv`, `integral_mean_mul_eq_stForm_swap`). Wrappers:
  4441	`space_time_positivity_homog` (all facts under `H:homog` with `a = alpha0`,
  4442	`Gamma != 0` not assumed); `spaceTimeCS_holds` (the proposition `SpaceTimeCS
  4443	alpha0 Gamma`, whose fields are definitionally those of

  4446	`positive_raw_variance_form_paper` with the sections' standing assumptions

  4450	supported fields `g` in place of the class `O` (no unit-norm condition is

  4453	by `sqrt(v_Psi A(g))`); for `L:positive-raw-embedding`, only the variance
  4454	identity `F(Psi,Psi) = v_Psi` with integrability and `v_Psi >= 0`. Not

  4456	`||rho_g||^2 = A(g)`; `H_t`, `H_I`, `J_G` and its bound by `K_0` (the scalar
  4457	Schur bound is `OccupationCeilingFinite.schur_sharp`); the mean identity
  4458	`T_R Psi(s) = B_E(m_R h_(Psi,s))` and the canonical versions of
  4459	`L:positive-raw-embedding`. Supplied inputs: none.

  4462	reliance: `CSConstant` (the constant `1/2` in the Cauchy-Schwarz bound

5568	## StaticPhaseCauchy (whole result)
  5569	
  5570	Formalizes the complex-analytic, scalar and Banach-space steps of the proof
  5571	of `P:static-phase-all-orders` (All regularized static phase orders) of
  5572	`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420` (main TeX;
  5573	statement lines 2577-2605, proof lines 2607-2683; all line numbers in this
  5574	section refer to that file). The proposition is an operator and stochastic
  5575	statement. Every row below is either a step proved with nothing supplied or
  5576	a step row of `E:all-static-phase-orders` (lines 2589-2595) or
  5577	`E:all-static-phase-sum` (lines 2599-2604) whose operator and Gaussian
  5578	inputs are supplied hypotheses (class inputs supplied, conclusion weaker
  5579	than the labelled statement). It extends the existing proof-step rows of
  5580	`SeriesType` for this proposition (the elementary series bound of lines
  5581	2670-2679), which `all_static_phase_sum_step` uses.
  5582	
  5583	Constants (nothing supplied): `I_a` and `delta_a = min{1/4, pi/(8 I_a)}` of
  5584	`L:complex-phase` (lines 2298-2299), with `I_a` proved integrable and
  5585	positive for `a < 2` (the TeX uses `a = alpha/2` in `(0,1)`), so `delta_a`
  5586	is a genuine positive number; `A_alpha = 400 sqrt(2) e^2/delta_(alpha/2)`
  5587	(lines 2585-2587); `d_N = 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(R_alpha)` of `E:fock-sandwich`
  5588	(lines 2484-2488).
  5589	
  5590	Steps (nothing supplied): Cauchy's estimate for an entire map with values
  5591	in a complete complex normed space, operator-valued included (lines
  5592	2616-2624), and the coefficient bound `||C_n|| <= M (d/c)^n` in the TeX's
  5593	form, quantified over every `d' >= d`, `d' > 0` (this covers the TeX's
  5594	`R_alpha = 0` case of line 2608 without dividing by zero); the arithmetic at
  5595	`lambda = n/h` (lines 2631-2641): `d_n <= 2 sqrt(2n) sqrt(R)`, the display of
  5596	lines 2636-2638, `100 n <= 200^n`, `n! <= n^n`; the pointwise Fourier
  5597	multiplier form of the norm comparisons of lines 2632-2633 (the integration
  5598	against the Fourier transform is not formalized); the exponent identity of
  5599	`E:all-static-phase-sum`.
  5600	
  5601	Step rows. `E:all-static-phase-orders` at fixed cutoffs
  5602	(`static_phase_order_cutoff`) and after both cutoff removals
  5603	(`static_phase_all_orders_step`, wrapper `static_phase_all_orders_paper`),
  5604	and `E:all-static-phase-sum` (`all_static_phase_sum_step`, wrapper
  5605	`all_static_phase_sum_paper`). Abstractions: a complex Banach space stands
  5606	for the cutoff space `L^2(Omega; X_lambda)` and a real Banach space for
  5607	`L^2(Omega; X_(1/h))`; the phase propagator is an entire map `F` from the
  5608	complex coupling to the bounded operators, its argument `v` is the initial
  5609	phase `S_b(f,g)` times the vacuum, and the phase norms are real numbers
  5610	`z1`, `zc m b`, `z`, `N1` named by the inputs. The supplied inputs are:
  5611	entireness of the phase entries in the coupling (lines 2616-2617); the
  5612	circle bound `100 e^(2 lambda h)` from `L:fock-form` and `L:complex-phase`
  5613	with `a = alpha/2` (lines 2611-2614), stated for every `d' >= d_n`,
  5614	`d' > 0`, which `L:complex-phase` gives from the sandwich bound of
  5615	`L:fock-form` (a sandwich bound with constant `d_N` holds with every larger
  5616	constant); the identification of the coefficient with the cutoff Duhamel
  5617	phase via `L:finite-word-cutoff` (lines 2625-2630) together with the norm
  5618	comparison `||z||_(1/h) <= n ||z||_(n/h)` (line 2632); `||S_b(f,g)||_(n/h) <=
  5619	||(f,g)||_(1/h)` (line 2633; the contraction `||S_b(f,g)||_lambda <=
  5620	||(f,g)||_lambda` is implicit in the TeX); the cutoff removals `b ->
  5621	infinity` and `m -> infinity` (lines 2643-2667) as convergence of the norms
  5622	along natural-number cutoffs (the TeX proves strong convergence, which

  5626	The wrappers state the section's standing class as in

  5629	sin(pi alpha/2))`; evenness, positive definiteness and scaling of `Gamma`

  5633	(the step holds for every real `R` and `alpha < 2`); in
  5634	`all_static_phase_sum_paper`, local finiteness (`0 < alpha` and the formula

  5636	
  5637	Junk values: `delta_a` is not a junk value (`I_a` is a proved-integrable
  5638	positive integral); every real power has a positive base or a nonnegative
  5639	base with a positive exponent; there is no division by `d_N`; summability
  5640	is proved, not assumed through `tsum`. `sqrt(R)` is the real square root;
  5641	in the wrappers `R = R_alpha >= 0`.
  5642	
  5643	Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the regularized Duhamel phases
  5644	`Z_n^eps(h)` themselves, their being Gaussian polynomials of degree at most
  5645	`n`, the uniformity in `eps` (it is that of the inputs), the convergence of

  5647	series (Lean proves absolute convergence of the abstract series), and the
  5648	lemmas `L:fock-form`, `L:complex-phase` and the cutoff-removal arguments.
  5649	The conclusions are the two displays for the quantities named by the

5683	## SymplecticFree (whole result)
  5684	
  5685	Formalizes the abstract core of `L:symplectic-free` (Free wave form and
  5686	compact Young baseline) of `notes/integrated_symplectic_phase.tex` at
  5687	`a284420` (statement lines 30-60, proof lines 62-133; all line numbers in
  5688	this section refer to that file). The lemma is an operator statement on
  5689	`E = H^(1/2) x H^(-1/2)`; every row below is either a finite or
  5690	operator-theoretic step proved with nothing supplied, or a statement about
  5691	the free group that takes the supplied structure `FreeWaveData` (class
  5692	inputs supplied, conclusion weaker than the labelled statement).
  5693	
  5694	What is formalized. (1) The per-frequency free matrix `W_t(xi)` of lines
  5695	70-78 (`freeMatrix`, `freeMatrixAt`), written with the continuous sine
  5696	quotient `t sinc(tk)` so that its value at `xi = 0` is the TeX's matrix
  5697	`[[1, t], [0, 1]]`; determinant one and `W_t^T J_symp W_t = J_symp` at every
  5698	frequency, zero included (lines 79-81), the per-frequency group law and the
  5699	reversal identity `R W_t R = W_(-t)` (lines 120-122). At nonzero frequency
  5700	the matrix is the forward matrix of `DimensionalMatrix`
  5701	(`freeMatrix_eq_forward`). (2) The force skewness of lines 40-41 and 88-91:
  5702	abstractly for a bilinear pairing that is symmetric through the force
  5703	(`omega_force_skew`), and at the `L^2` level on `R^d` with the integrability
  5704	of the cancellation integrand (`omegaL2_force_skew`,
  5705	`integrable_mul_force`). (3) The operator steps of the two compact
  5706	baselines: closedness of the compact ideal along a nontrivial filter, each
  5707	left Young sum compact, telescoping of ordered products, a compact operator
  5708	maps a bounded weakly null family to a norm-null one, the abstract bound
  5709	`||S|| <= ||S + K||` for `S` commuting with weakly null isometries, and
  5710	`1 <= ||A||` from `B A = I`, `B = R A R`. (4) The two displays
  5711	`E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline` (lines 45-49) and
  5712	`E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline` (lines 53-58) in general form and as
  5713	exact-hypothesis wrappers, and their conjunction with the per-frequency
  5714	identity and the `L^2` force skewness (`symplectic_free_paper`).
  5715	
  5716	Abstractions and supplied inputs. `E` is an abstract nonzero real Hilbert
  5717	space. `FreeWaveData d E` (D8) carries the free group `S_E` (`S_E(0) = I`,
  5718	group law), an isometry `R` with `S_E(-h) = R S_E(h) R`, and isometries
  5719	`tau_y`, `y` in `R^d`, commuting with every `S_E(h)` and weakly null along
  5720	the cocompact filter of `R^d`: exactly the properties that lines 103-122
  5721	state for the free wave group, the velocity reversal `(u,v) -> (u,-v)` and
  5722	the spatial translations (the weak nullity is the Riemann-Lebesgue argument
  5723	of lines 105-110). `LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t` (D7) stands for
  5724	`P:constant-young-linear` applied on `L(E)` (lines 91-98): along some
  5725	nontrivial filter of finite node lists `(n, p)` whose nodes `p 0, ..., p n`
  5726	lie eventually in `[s,t]`, the left Young sums of `X` converge in operator
  5727	norm to `U(t,s) - I`. The node lists need not be partitions: ordered nodes,
  5728	the endpoints `p 0 = s`, `p n = t` and a vanishing mesh are not required, so
  5729	the condition does not characterize the Young evolution; convergence as the
  5730	mesh of genuine partitions tends to zero implies it, so it is no stronger
  5731	than its source. The Young evolution
  5732	itself is not constructed: `U` is any operator family with this property.
  5733	The wrappers take `H:homog` as the standing hypothesis; it is used only
  5734	through `d >= 1`.
  5735	
  5736	Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `E != 0` (on the zero space every
  5737	operator has norm `0`, and `||S_E(h)|| >= 1` fails), `d >= 1` (from
  5738	`H:homog`; it makes the cocompact filter nontrivial), and the nodes lying
  5739	in `[s,t]`. Hypotheses carried but unused (stated in the
  5740	wrappers' doc comments and confirmed by their proofs): `theta`, the Hoelder
  5741	bounds and `X(0) = 0` (they are the hypotheses of the supplied Young input)
  5742	in both baseline wrappers, and `T > 0` in the single-path wrapper
  5743	`symplectic_compact_young_baseline_paper` (the product wrapper has the
  5744	horizon `B` and no positivity hypothesis); `H:homog` and smoothness beyond
  5745	continuity in `symplectic_force_skew_paper`.
  5746	
  5747	Proof-route differences: the compact-maps-weakly-null step (lines 110-112)
  5748	is proved along an arbitrary filter through cluster points in the compact
  5749	closure of the image of a ball and the adjoint, not by subsequences; the
  5750	norm bound of lines 114-119 is proved for each `z` by a limit along the
  5751	filter; the per-frequency symplecticity goes through `M^T J_symp M = (det M)
  5752	J_symp` for every `2 x 2` matrix. Helpers that serve only this route are
  5753	labelled auxiliary.
  5754	
  5755	Narrower than the TeX, and not formalized: the operator `J_E` (bounded,
  5756	isometric, skew-adjoint, `J_E^2 = -I`), the identity `omega = <., J_E .>_E`
  5757	with its duality form (lines 32-39, 63-68), the preservation of `omega` by
  5758	`S_E` on all of `E` (the Fourier integration of the per-frequency identity,
  5759	lines 82-86), the identification of the `H^(1/2)`-`H^(-1/2)` duality with
  5760	the `L^2` integral and the estimate `||bu||_(H^(-1/2)) <=
  5761	||b||_infinity ||u||_(H^(1/2))` (line 88), the construction of `S_E`,
  5762	`tau_y` and the reversal with the properties of `FreeWaveData`, the Young
  5763	evolution, and the remark that a zero length gives `P_j = I` (lines 129-130).
  5764	The two displays are stated exactly as in the TeX, for the supplied objects.

   100	/-! ### Per-frequency free matrix -/
   128	/-- The continuous sine quotient `t ↦ sin(tk)/k`, with value `t` at `k = 0`:
   129	`sineQuotient t k = t · sinc(tk)`. -/
   130	def sineQuotient (t k : ℝ) : ℝ := t * Real.sinc (t * k)
   131	
   132	/-- Auxiliary: `sineQuotient t k = sin(tk)/k` for `k ≠ 0`. -/
   133	theorem sineQuotient_of_ne_zero (t : ℝ) {k : ℝ} (hk : k ≠ 0) :
   134	    sineQuotient t k = Real.sin (t * k) / k := by
   135	  unfold sineQuotient
   136	  by_cases ht : t = 0
   137	  · simp [ht]
   138	  · rw [Real.sinc_of_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero ht hk)]
   139	    field_simp
   140	
   141	/-- Auxiliary: `sineQuotient t 0 = t`. -/
   142	theorem sineQuotient_zero (t : ℝ) : sineQuotient t 0 = t := by
   143	  simp [sineQuotient]
   144	
   145	/-- Auxiliary: `sineQuotient t k · k = sin(tk)`, every `k`. -/
   146	theorem sineQuotient_mul (t k : ℝ) : sineQuotient t k * k = Real.sin (t * k) := by
   147	  by_cases hk : k = 0
   148	  · simp [hk]
   149	  · rw [sineQuotient_of_ne_zero t hk]
   150	    field_simp
   151	
   152	/-- The sine quotient is continuous in `k` (the "continuous sine quotient", line 79). -/
   153	theorem continuous_sineQuotient (t : ℝ) : Continuous (fun k => sineQuotient t k) := by
   154	  unfold sineQuotient
   155	  fun_prop
   156	
   157	/-- Auxiliary: `sineQuotient (-t) k = -sineQuotient t k`. -/
   158	theorem sineQuotient_neg (t k : ℝ) : sineQuotient (-t) k = -sineQuotient t k := by
   159	  simp [sineQuotient, neg_mul, Real.sinc_neg]
   160	
   161	/-- The free matrix in balanced Fourier coordinates (TeX lines 70-77), with
   162	frequency modulus `k = |ξ|` and weight `br = ⟨ξ⟩`; the `(0,1)` entry uses
   163	the continuous sine quotient, so the matrix at `k = 0` is the TeX's limit. -/
   164	def freeMatrix (t k br : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ :=
   165	  !![Real.cos (t * k), br * sineQuotient t k; -(k * Real.sin (t * k)) / br, Real.cos (t * k)]
   166	
   167	/-- The free matrix at the frequency `ξ ∈ ℝ^d`: `k = |ξ|`, `⟨ξ⟩ = √(1+|ξ|²)`. -/
   168	def freeMatrixAt {d : ℕ} (t : ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ :=
   169	  freeMatrix t ‖ξ‖ (Real.sqrt (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2))
   170	
   171	/-- Auxiliary: `⟨ξ⟩ = √(1+|ξ|²) > 0`. -/
   172	theorem bracket_pos {d : ℕ} (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) : 0 < Real.sqrt (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) :=
   173	  Real.sqrt_pos.2 (by positivity)
   174	
   175	/-- At nonzero frequency the free matrix is the B22 matrix
   176	`DimensionalMatrix.forward (cos tk) (sin tk) (k/⟨ξ⟩)`. -/
   177	theorem freeMatrix_eq_forward (t : ℝ) {k br : ℝ} (hk : k ≠ 0) (hbr : br ≠ 0) :
   178	    freeMatrix t k br =
   179	      StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.forward (Real.cos (t * k)) (Real.sin (t * k))
   180	        (k / br) := by
   181	  rw [freeMatrix, StratonovichHAMAudit.DimensionalMatrix.forward,
   182	    sineQuotient_of_ne_zero t hk]
   183	  ext i j
   184	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp <;> field_simp
   185	
   186	/-- At frequency zero the free matrix is `!![1, br t; 0, 1]` (TeX line 78 with `⟨0⟩ = 1`). -/
   187	theorem freeMatrix_zero_freq (t br : ℝ) : freeMatrix t 0 br = !![1, br * t; 0, 1] := by
   188	  simp [freeMatrix, sineQuotient_zero]
   189	
   190	/-- `W_t(0) = (1 t; 0 1)` (TeX line 78). -/
   191	theorem freeMatrixAt_zero {d : ℕ} (t : ℝ) :
   192	    freeMatrixAt t (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) = !![1, t; 0, 1] := by
   193	  simp [freeMatrixAt, freeMatrix_zero_freq]
   194	
   195	/-- The entries of the free matrix are continuous in the frequency modulus `k`
   196	(fixed `t` and `br`), the frequency-zero value included. -/
   197	theorem continuous_freeMatrix (t br : ℝ) :
   198	    Continuous (fun k => freeMatrix t k br) := by
   199	  refine continuous_pi fun i => continuous_pi fun j => ?_
   200	  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [freeMatrix]
   201	  · fun_prop
   202	  · exact continuous_const.mul (continuous_sineQuotient t)
   203	  · fun_prop
   204	  · fun_prop
   205	
   206	/-- Determinant one at every frequency, also at zero (TeX lines 80-81). -/
   207	theorem det_freeMatrix (t k : ℝ) {br : ℝ} (hbr : br ≠ 0) : (freeMatrix t k br).det = 1 := by
   208	  rw [Matrix.det_fin_two]
   209	  simp only [freeMatrix, Matrix.of_apply, Matrix.cons_val', Matrix.cons_val_zero,
   210	    Matrix.cons_val_one, Matrix.empty_val', Matrix.cons_val_fin_one]
   211	  have h1 := sineQuotient_mul t k
   212	  have h2 : br * sineQuotient t k * (-(k * Real.sin (t * k)) / br)
   213	      = -(sineQuotient t k * k) * Real.sin (t * k) := by
   214	    field_simp
   215	  rw [h2, h1]
   216	  nlinarith [Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq (t * k)]
   217	
   218	/-- Per-frequency symplecticity `W_tᵀ J_symp W_t = J_symp` (TeX lines 79-81), at
   219	every frequency modulus `k`, zero included, for every weight `br ≠ 0`. -/
   220	theorem freeMatrix_symplectic (t k : ℝ) {br : ℝ} (hbr : br ≠ 0) :
   221	    (freeMatrix t k br)ᵀ * Jsymp * freeMatrix t k br = Jsymp := by
   222	  rw [transpose_mul_Jsymp_mul, det_freeMatrix t k hbr, one_smul]
   223	
   224	/-- `W_t(ξ)ᵀ J_symp W_t(ξ) = J_symp` at every `ξ ∈ ℝ^d`, `ξ = 0` included. -/
   225	theorem freeMatrixAt_symplectic {d : ℕ} (t : ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
   226	    (freeMatrixAt t ξ)ᵀ * Jsymp * freeMatrixAt t ξ = Jsymp :=
   227	  freeMatrix_symplectic t ‖ξ‖ (bracket_pos ξ).ne'
   228	
   229	/-- The free matrix preserves the per-frequency form: `ω₂(W_t z, W_t w) = ω₂(z,w)`. -/
   230	theorem freeMatrix_preserves_omega2 (t k : ℝ) {br : ℝ} (hbr : br ≠ 0) (z w : Fin 2 → ℝ) :
   231	    omega2 (freeMatrix t k br *ᵥ z) (freeMatrix t k br *ᵥ w) = omega2 z w := by
   232	  rw [omega2_mulVec, det_freeMatrix t k hbr, one_mul]
   233	
   234	/-- Per-frequency group law `W_s W_t = W_{s+t}` (the frequency form of the group law of
   235	the free group used in TeX lines 101 and 121-122). -/
   236	theorem freeMatrix_mul (s t k : ℝ) {br : ℝ} (hbr : br ≠ 0) :
   237	    freeMatrix s k br * freeMatrix t k br = freeMatrix (s + t) k br := by
   238	  by_cases hk : k = 0
   239	  · subst hk
   240	    simp only [freeMatrix_zero_freq]

   514	/-! ### Supplied inputs and the wrappers -/
   515	
   516	/-- Supplied input (D8; TeX lines 103-122): the free wave group `S_E` on
   517	`E = H^{1/2} × H^{-1/2}`, the velocity reversal `𝓡(u,v) = (u,-v)` and the spatial
   518	translations `τ_y`, `y ∈ ℝ^d`, with the properties the proof of `L:symplectic-free`
   519	states for them: the group law, `S_E(-h) = 𝓡 S_E(h) 𝓡` with `𝓡` isometric,
   520	translations isometric and commuting with `S_E(h)`, and `⟨τ_y z, w⟩_E → 0` as
   521	`|y| → ∞` (cocompact filter on `ℝ^d`). -/
   522	structure FreeWaveData (d : ℕ) (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] where
   523	  /-- The free group `S_E(t)`. -/
   524	  S : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E
   525	  S_zero : S 0 = 1
   526	  S_add : ∀ s t, S (s + t) = S s * S t
   527	  /-- The velocity reversal. -/
   528	  R : E →L[ℝ] E
   529	  R_norm : ∀ z, ‖R z‖ = ‖z‖
   530	  S_neg : ∀ h, S (-h) = R * S h * R
   531	  /-- The translations `τ_y`. -/
   532	  τ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → E →L[ℝ] E
   533	  τ_norm : ∀ y z, ‖τ y z‖ = ‖z‖
   534	  τ_comm : ∀ y h, S h * τ y = τ y * S h
   535	  τ_weak : ∀ z w, Tendsto (fun y => inner ℝ (τ y z) w) (cocompact (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) (𝓝 0)
   536	
   537	/-- Supplied input (D7; `P:constant-young-linear` on `𝓛(E)`, TeX lines 91-98): the left
   538	Young sums of `X` over partitions of `[s,t]` converge in operator norm to
   539	`U(t,s) - I` along some nontrivial filter of partitions.  A partition is a pair
   540	`(n, p)` with points `p 0, …, p n`; only the points `p j`, `j ≤ n`, enter, and they lie
   541	in `[s,t]` eventually.  The TeX's convergence as the mesh tends to zero implies this
   542	statement (the mesh filter is nontrivial). -/
   543	def LeftYoungSumsConverge {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
   544	    (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (U : ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (s t : ℝ) : Prop :=
   545	  ∃ l : Filter (ℕ × (ℕ → ℝ)), l.NeBot ∧
   546	    (∀ᶠ π in l, ∀ j ≤ π.1, π.2 j ∈ Set.Icc s t) ∧
   547	    Tendsto (fun π => youngSum X U s π.2 π.1) l (𝓝 (U t s - 1))

   551	variable {d : ℕ} {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
   552	
   553	/-- Auxiliary: for `d ≥ 1` the cocompact filter of `ℝ^d` is nontrivial. -/
   554	theorem FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
   555	    (cocompact (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))).NeBot := by
   556	  have : Nonempty (Fin d) := ⟨⟨0, hd⟩⟩
   557	  infer_instance
   558	
   559	omit [CompleteSpace E] in
   560	/-- `‖S_E(h)‖ ≥ 1` (TeX lines 120-122), for a nonzero `E`. -/
   561	theorem FreeWaveData.one_le_norm [Nontrivial E] (F : FreeWaveData d E) (h : ℝ) :
   562	    1 ≤ ‖F.S h‖ :=
   563	  one_le_norm_of_reversal (F.S h) (F.S (-h)) F.R
   564	    (by rw [← F.S_add, neg_add_cancel, F.S_zero]) F.R_norm (F.S_neg h)
   565	
   566	/-- `‖S_E(h)‖ ≤ ‖S_E(h) + K‖` for every compact `K` (TeX lines 103-119), `d ≥ 1`. -/
   567	theorem FreeWaveData.norm_le_norm_add_compact (F : FreeWaveData d E) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (h : ℝ)
   568	    (K : E →L[ℝ] E) (hK : IsCompactOperator K) : ‖F.S h‖ ≤ ‖F.S h + K‖ := by
   569	  have := FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot hd
   570	  exact SymplecticFree.norm_le_norm_add_compact (cocompact _) (F.S h) F.τ F.τ_norm
   571	    (fun y => F.τ_comm y h) (fun z w => F.τ_weak z w) K hK
   572	
   573	/-- The compact Young baseline in general form: if the left Young sums of `X` over
   574	partitions of `[s,t]` converge to `U(t,s) - I` (supplied, D7) and `X` is compact on
   575	`[s,t]`, then `U(t,s) - I` and `S_E(t) U(t,s) S_E(-s) - S_E(t-s)` are compact, and
   576	`‖S_E(t) U(t,s) S_E(-s)‖ ≥ ‖S_E(t-s)‖ ≥ 1`. -/
   577	theorem compact_young_baseline [Nontrivial E] (F : FreeWaveData d E) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
   578	    (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (U : ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (s t : ℝ)
   579	    (hXK : ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc s t, IsCompactOperator (X r))
   580	    (hY : LeftYoungSumsConverge X U s t) :
   581	    IsCompactOperator ⇑(U t s - 1 : E →L[ℝ] E) ∧
   582	      IsCompactOperator (F.S t * U t s * F.S (-s) - F.S (t - s)) ∧
   583	      ‖F.S (t - s)‖ ≤ ‖F.S t * U t s * F.S (-s)‖ ∧ 1 ≤ ‖F.S (t - s)‖ := by
   584	  obtain ⟨l, hl, hpts, hlim⟩ := hY
   585	  have hU : IsCompactOperator ⇑(U t s - 1 : E →L[ℝ] E) := by
   586	    refine isCompactOperator_of_tendsto hlim ?_
   587	    filter_upwards [hpts] with π hπ
   588	    exact isCompactOperator_youngSum X U s π.2 π.1 fun j hj => hXK _ (hπ j hj)
   589	  have hdiff : F.S t * U t s * F.S (-s) - F.S (t - s) = F.S t * (U t s - 1) * F.S (-s) := by
   590	    rw [sub_eq_add_neg t s, F.S_add, mul_sub, sub_mul, mul_one]
   591	  have hK : IsCompactOperator (F.S t * U t s * F.S (-s) - F.S (t - s)) := by
   592	    rw [hdiff]
   593	    exact isCompactOperator_mul_right (isCompactOperator_mul_left _ hU) _
   594	  have := FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot hd
   595	  refine ⟨hU, hK, ?_, F.one_le_norm _⟩
   596	  exact norm_le_of_sub_compact (cocompact _) (F.S (t - s)) _ F.τ F.τ_norm
   597	    (fun y => F.τ_comm y _) (fun z w => F.τ_weak z w) hK
   598	
   599	omit [CompleteSpace E] in
   600	/-- Auxiliary: the free product `S_E(ℓ_N) ⋯ S_E(ℓ_0) = S_E(∑_{j ≤ N} ℓ_j)` (group law). -/
   601	theorem FreeWaveData.orderedProd_S (F : FreeWaveData d E) (ℓ : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
   602	    orderedProd (fun j => F.S (ℓ j)) N = F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j) := by
   603	  induction N with
   604	  | zero => simp [orderedProd]
   605	  | succ n ih =>
   606	    rw [orderedProd, ih, ← F.S_add]
   607	    congr 1
   608	    rw [Finset.sum_range_succ _ (n + 1)]
   609	    ring
   610	
   611	/-- The compact product baseline in general form: if each `U_j(ℓ_j,0) - I` is compact,
   612	`P_j = S_E(ℓ_j) U_j(ℓ_j,0)`, then `P_N ⋯ P_0 - S_E(∑ ℓ_j)` is compact and
   613	`‖P_N ⋯ P_0‖ ≥ ‖S_E(∑ ℓ_j)‖ ≥ 1`. -/
   614	theorem compact_product_baseline [Nontrivial E] (F : FreeWaveData d E) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
   615	    (U : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (ℓ : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ)
   616	    (hU : ∀ j ≤ N, IsCompactOperator ⇑(U j (ℓ j) 0 - 1 : E →L[ℝ] E)) :
   617	    IsCompactOperator (orderedProd (fun j => F.S (ℓ j) * U j (ℓ j) 0) N
   618	        - F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j)) ∧
   619	      ‖F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j)‖
   620	        ≤ ‖orderedProd (fun j => F.S (ℓ j) * U j (ℓ j) 0) N‖ ∧
   621	      1 ≤ ‖F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j)‖ := by
   622	  have hK : IsCompactOperator (orderedProd (fun j => F.S (ℓ j) * U j (ℓ j) 0) N
   623	      - F.S (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), ℓ j)) := by
   624	    rw [← F.orderedProd_S ℓ N]
   625	    refine isCompactOperator_orderedProd_sub _ _ N fun j hj => ?_
   626	    have : F.S (ℓ j) * U j (ℓ j) 0 - F.S (ℓ j) = F.S (ℓ j) * (U j (ℓ j) 0 - 1) := by
   627	      rw [mul_sub, mul_one]
   628	    rw [this]
   629	    exact isCompactOperator_mul_left _ (hU j hj)
   630	  have := FreeWaveData.cocompact_neBot hd
   631	  refine ⟨hK, ?_, F.one_le_norm _⟩
   632	  exact norm_le_of_sub_compact (cocompact _) _ _ F.τ F.τ_norm
   633	    (fun y => F.τ_comm y _) (fun z w => F.τ_weak z w) hK

   681	theorem symplectic_compact_product_baseline_paper [Nontrivial E]

1	\section{A variational formula for the second-moment limit}
     2	\label{S:intrinsic-second-moment}
     3	
     4	Retain every original covariance and amplitude. Write $a = \alpha_0$, $I =
     5	(0,1)$, $K(s,t) = |s-t|^{-a}$ and $H_I = H_t\otimes H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ for the
     6	original covariance. Keep the uniform $E$ mean $\mathcal{T}_R = T_R(C_t\otimes
     7	I)$ and $C_{\rm mean} = M_0\|C_t\|$ of
     8	Section~\ref{S:uniform-physical-products}, with exactly the fixed $r$ chosen
     9	there. In particular, $2 < r < 2/a$. To distinguish it from the map below, write
    10	$J_R = T_R$. For a bounded multiplier $V:H^{1/2} \to H^{-1/2}$ write
    11	$B_E(V)(u,v) = (0,Vu)$, the $E$ operator of Lemma~\ref{L:uniform-E-lift}. The
    12	physical mask is $m_R = \eta(\cdot/R)^2$, used once. Let
    13	$\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$ be the full nonseparable class
    14	in~\eqref{E:variational-positive-class}. For $\Psi$ in that class, retain its
    15	unmasked mean $h_{\Psi,s}$, original variance $v_\Psi$, integrated full-gradient
    16	rate $I_\Psi$ and variational values for nonnegative controls
    17	$S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ from Section~\ref{S:unmasked-variational}. The value with
    18	coefficient one is not identified with a first-moment limit or a constant in the
    19	cited source. We assume $\Gamma \ne 0$ through the following comparison lemmas.
    20	The theorem treats zero covariance directly.
    21	
    22	\begin{lemma}[Inclusion into the covariance space and the smooth mean]
    23	  \label{L:positive-raw-embedding}
    24	  For any real Hilbert space $G$ there is a bounded map $J_G:L^2(I;G) \to
    25	  H_t\otimes G$ with
    26	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-bochner-inclusion}
    27	    \|J_GF\|^2
    28	    =\int_{I^2}K(s,t)\langle F(s),F(t)\rangle_G\ud s\ud t
    29	    \le K_0\|F\|_{L^2(I;G)}^2,\qquad K_0=\frac{2^a}{1-a}.
    30	  \end{equation}
    31	  The natural inclusion puts every $\Psi \in \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}$ in
    32	  $H_I$, with
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-raw-mean}
    34	    \|\Psi\|_{H_I}^2=v_\Psi,\qquad
    35	    \mathcal{T}_R\Psi(s)=B_E(m_Rh_{\Psi,s})\quad\hbox{a.e. }s.
    36	  \end{equation}
    37	  For each fixed smooth $\Psi$ the right side gives a canonical version for
    38	  every $R \ge 1$ and every $s \in I$.
    39	\end{lemma}
    40	
    41	\begin{proof}
    42	  Direct integration and concavity of $x^{1-a}$ give
    43	  \[
    44	    \int_I K(s,t)\ud t
    45	    =\frac{s^{1-a}+(1-s)^{1-a}}{1-a}\le K_0 .
    46	  \]
    47	  For scalar $f \ge 0$, Cauchy--Schwarz against $K(s,t)\ud t$ and then Tonelli
    48	  give $\|Kf\|_2 \le K_0\|f\|_2$. The same estimate for absolute values bounds
    49	  the bilinear integral by $K_0\|f\|_2\|g\|_2$. Approximate scalar $L^2(I)$
    50	  functions by real $C_c^\infty(I)$ functions. This bound makes their original
    51	  test-null classes Cauchy in $H_t$, defines the bounded inclusion, and
    52	  identifies its pairing with the integral. Finite $G$-valued tensors then give
    53	  \eqref{E:positive-bochner-inclusion}. Simple fields are dense in Bochner
    54	  $L^2(I;G)$; the same bound on differences extends $J_G$. Absolute bilinear
    55	  continuity extends the integral identity as well.
    56	
    57	  For $G = H_{\mathrm{sp}}$, the Bochner integral $\int_IK(s,t)F(t)\ud t$ exists
    58	  almost everywhere: its norm is bounded by $K\|F\|(s)$, which belongs to $L^2$.
    59	  Simple-field approximation and the Schur estimate give a strongly measurable
    60	  $L^2$ version and a bounded map of norm at most $K_0$. On smooth finite
    61	  tensors it agrees with $(C_t\otimes I)J_G$ by the covariance definition.
    62	  Approximation by such tensors converges in $L^2(I;G)$. The integral converges
    63	  there by Schur; the completed tensor map converges in $L^r(I;G)$ by
    64	  Lemma~\ref{L:uniform-mean-tensor} and~\eqref{E:positive-bochner-inclusion},
    65	  hence also in $L^2$. Uniqueness of the $L^2$ limit identifies these versions.
    66	  In particular, the integral belongs to $L^r$.
    67	
    68	  Choose a closed ball $B$ containing all spatial supports of $\Psi$. For real
    69	  smooth $q$ supported there, the physical covariance gives
    70	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-local-spatial-bound}
    71	    \|q\|_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}^2
    72	    \le |B|\,\Gamma(B-B)\|q\|_\infty^2.
    73	  \end{equation}
    74	  Indeed, in $\int\ud x\int\Gamma(\ud y)q(x)q(x-y)$ only $x \in B,y \in B-B$
    75	  contribute. Absolute values and local finiteness prove the bound, including
    76	  white and singular Radon covariances. Thus, $t\mapsto\Psi_t$ is continuous,
    77	  bounded and compactly supported as an $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$-valued field, and
    78	  belongs to $L^2$. Its image under $J_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}$ is the original test
    79	  class of $\Psi$. Indeed, the separated compact smooth approximants in
    80	  Lemma~\ref{L:cameron-supported-tensor} converge uniformly on one common
    81	  compact support. The local bound above and the temporal Schur estimate give
    82	  convergence both in $L^2(I;H_{\mathrm{sp}})$ and in the original covariance
    83	  norm. Their finite tensor identifications therefore have this same limit.
    84	  Formula~\eqref{E:positive-bochner-inclusion} and absolute Fubini give
    85	  \[
    86	    \|\Psi\|_{H_I}^2
    87	    =\int_{I^2}K(s,t)\langle\Psi_s,\Psi_t\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    88	    \ud s\ud t
    89	    =\int_{I\times\R^d}\Psi(s,x)h_{\Psi,s}(x)\ud x\ud s=v_\Psi.
    90	  \]
    91	  The compact spatial supports and~\eqref{E:positive-local-spatial-bound} make
    92	  all these absolute integrals finite.
    93	
    94	  Test the spatial row~\eqref{E:uniform-mean-row} first with displacement $f$
    95	  and dual second component $\Lambda g$, with $f,g$ compact smooth. The row
    96	  product is $m_Rfg$, so the preceding temporal identity gives
    97	  \[
    98	    \left\langle\int_IK(s,t)\Psi_t\ud t,m_Rfg\right\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    99	    =\int m_Rh_{\Psi,s}fg .
   100	  \]
   101	  This Fubini step has two fixed compact supports and integrable time kernel.
   102	  Both resulting operators are bounded on $E$: the left by the mean theorem, the

    82	  bounded on finite time horizons. Integrating the identity against real-phase
    83	  Fourier vectors with Hermitian symmetry is legitimate by $L^2$

    88	  Finally, $\|bu\|_{H^{-1/2}} \le \|bu\|_2 \le \|b\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^{1/2}}$.

   175	\subsection{The exact linear Young equation}
   176	
   177	We use Young's integration theory~\cite{young:36:inequality} in its
   178	Banach-space form. The estimate is stated by
   179	Friz and Hairer~\cite{friz.hairer:20:course}*{Sections~1.4--1.5, 4.1, (4.3), pp.~13, 61--62}.
   180	For $D,V$ with exponent $\theta > 1/2$ and bounded bilinear multiplication, left
   181	composition gives
   182	\begin{equation}\label{E:constant-young-estimate}
   183	  \left\|\int_s^t\ud D(r)V(r)-D(s,t)V(s)\right\|
   184	  \le C_\theta[D]_\theta[V]_\theta|t-s|^{2\theta}.
   185	\end{equation}
   186	The Banach spaces here are $\mathcal{B}(F)$, and multiplication is bounded with
   187	constant one. We derive the linear solution and stability estimates below rather
   188	than invoke a nonlinear bounded-vector-field theorem.
   189	
   190	\begin{proposition}[Linear Young evolution]\label{P:constant-young-linear}
   191	  For every $D \in C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{B}(F))$ with $D(0) = 0$ there is a
   192	  unique $C^\theta$ solution, in the terminal variable, of
   193	  \begin{equation}\label{E:constant-young-equation}
   194	    U_D(t,s)=I+\int_s^t\ud D(r)U_D(r,s).
   195	  \end{equation}
   196	  It has the composition law, invertible values and joint operator-norm
   197	  continuity on $0 \le s \le t \le T$. The map $D\mapsto U_D$ is locally
   198	  Lipschitz into the uniform time-triangle norm, and
   199	  \begin{equation}\label{E:constant-young-growth}
   200	    \sup_{s\le t\le T}\|U_D(t,s)\|
   201	    \le C_T\exp\big(C_T(1+\|D\|_{C^\theta})^{1/\theta}\big).
   202	  \end{equation}
   203	\end{proposition}
   204	
   205	\begin{proof}
   206	  On an interval $[a,a+\ell]$ use the complete scaled norm $N_\ell(V) =

161	  $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ into a finite product of $L^2$ spaces. Compact smooth
   162	  density therefore supplies a countable real family. Discard zero and normalize
   163	  each member in $L^2$ to obtain $f_j$ dense in the $L^2$-unit $H^1$ class.
   164	  Normalization preserves convergence because the approximating $L^2$ norms tend
   165	  to one. Put $b_j = \|\nabla f_j\|_2^2$ and $R_j(s) = \int
   166	  h_{\Psi,s}f_j^2-b_j$. Bounded-potential form continuity and
   167	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} give $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2 =
   168	  \sup_jR_j(s)$. The canonical functions are measurable, indeed continuous. Let
   169	  $U_j = \{s:R_j(s)>\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2-\varepsilon\}$, $A_1 = U_1$ and $A_j =
   170	  U_j\setminus\bigcup_{i<j}U_i$. These first-index cells are Borel and cover

   172	  $f_1$ on the remaining cells converge pointwise in $H^1$, proving strong

   177	    b(g_\varepsilon(s))

   190	  proves~\eqref{E:occupation-rayleigh-selection}. No eigenvector, continuum
   191	  selector or limiting occupation is required. This proves

  3583	\subsection{Finite Gaussian models and their terminal kernels}
  3584	
  3585	For $n \ge 1$, define the positive terminal-chain measure
  3586	\begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-chain-measure}
  3587	  \mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y)
  3588	  =\mathbf1_{[0,T]^n_<}(\boldsymbol s)\ud\boldsymbol s
  3589	  \prod_{j=1}^n
  3590	  G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(y_{j+1}-\ud y_j),
  3591	  \qquad (s_{n+1},y_{n+1})=(T,x).
  3592	\end{equation}
  3593	The spatial product is read backwards from $x$. Explicitly, it is the
  3594	pushforward of $\prod_{j=1}^nG_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(\ud w_j)$ under $y_j =
  3595	x-\sum_{l=j}^n w_l$. This defines the measure also in dimension three. In
  3596	dimensions one and two its density is the ordered kernel $g_n$
  3597	in~\eqref{E:expansion}. Set $\mathsf{g}_0^{T,x}$ equal to unit mass on the empty
  3598	tuple. This definition introduces no kernel symmetrization.
  3599	
  3600	\begin{lemma}[The finite terminal-chain Wick formula]\label{L:terminal-wick}
  3601	  Let $\mathcal{W}(s,y)$ be a centered real Gaussian field on $[0,T]\times\R^d$,
  3602	  $d = 1,2,3$, with covariance $\mathcal{K}(s,y;r,z)$. Suppose that $V =
  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and
  3606	  \[
  3607	    Y_n(T,x)=\int\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)
  3608	    \,\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}(\ud\boldsymbol s,\ud\boldsymbol y).
  3609	  \]
  3610	  These Bochner integrals exist in $L^2(\Omega)$ and satisfy
  3611	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-term-majorant}
  3612	    \|Y_n(T,x)\|_2
  3613	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}\frac{T^{2n}}{(2n)!},
  3614	    \qquad n\ge1.
  3615	  \end{equation}
  3616	  For $m+n = 2k$, concatenate $\boldsymbol\tau =
  3617	  (s_1,\ldots,s_m,r_1,\ldots,r_n)$ and $\boldsymbol\eta =
  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then
  3619	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-wick-formula}
  3620	    \E[Y_m(T,x)Y_n(T,x)]
  3621	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),
  3622	  \end{equation}
  3623	  where, with both chains terminating at $(T,x)$,
  3624	  \begin{equation}\label{E:terminal-pairing-integral}
  3625	    \begin{split}
  3626	      \mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}
  3627	      ={}&\int_{[0,T]^m_<\times[0,T]^n_<}
  3628	      \ud\boldsymbol s\,\ud\boldsymbol r
  3629	      \int_{(\R^d)^m\times(\R^d)^n}\\
  3630	      &\quad\times\prod_{j=1}^m
  3631	      G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(y_{j+1}-\ud y_j)
  3632	      \prod_{j=1}^n
  3633	      G_{r_{j+1}-r_j}(z_{j+1}-\ud z_j)\\
  3634	      &\quad\times\prod_{\{a,b\}\in D}
  3635	      \mathcal{K}(\tau_a,\eta_a;\tau_b,\eta_b).
  3636	    \end{split}
  3637	  \end{equation}
  3638	  Each pairing has coefficient one. If $m+n$ is odd, the expectation is zero.
  3639	  Empty chains and the case $m = n = 0$ have the usual empty-product meaning. If
  3640	  $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, every integral above is nonnegative. Consequently,
  3641	  entrywise comparison $0 \le \mathcal{K}_1 \le \mathcal{K}_2$ compares all
  3642	  finite partial-order second moments in the same direction. The series
  3643	  $\sum_{n\ge0}r^nY_n$ converges absolutely in $L^2$ for every real or complex
  3644	  $r$.
  3645	\end{lemma}
  3646	
  3647	\begin{proof}
  3648	  The mass of $G_h$ is $h$. If $M_n(T)$ is the total mass of
  3649	  $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$, integration at the last vertex gives $M_0 = 1$ and
  3650	  $M_n(T) = \int_0^T(T-s)M_{n-1}(s)\ud s$. Induction therefore yields $M_n(T) =
  3651	  T^{2n}/(2n)!$. Gaussian moments and H\"older's inequality give
  3652	  \[
  3653	    \left\|\prod_{j=1}^n\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\right\|_2
  3654	    \le\prod_{j=1}^n\|\mathcal{W}(s_j,y_j)\|_{2n}
  3655	    \le\sqrt{(2n-1)!!}\,V^{n/2}.
  3656	  \]
  3657	  Mean-square continuity of Gaussian variables implies their continuity in every
  3658	  fixed finite $L^p$. Hence, the product is strongly measurable in $L^2$ on the
  3659	  stated pieces. The finite kernel mass and the displayed bound prove Bochner
  3660	  integrability and~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}.
  3661	
  3662	  Fubini now passes expectation through the product of the two finite kernel
  3663	  measures. For the $m+n$ Gaussian variables at their labelled vertices,
  3664	  differentiate
  3665	  \[
  3666	    \E\exp\left(\sum_i t_i\mathcal{W}(\tau_i,\eta_i)\right)
  3667	    =\exp\left(\frac12\sum_{i,j}t_i t_j
  3668	    \mathcal{K}(\tau_i,\eta_i;\tau_j,\eta_j)\right)
  3669	  \]
  3670	  once in each $t_i$ at zero. Odd total degree gives zero. At degree $2k$ the
  3671	  result is the sum over unordered pair partitions, with one covariance product
  3672	  per pairing. Orientations and orderings of the $k$ pairs cancel the
  3673	  exponential's $2^k k!$ denominator. Integration
  3674	  gives~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula} with precisely the domains and
  3675	  coefficients in~\eqref{E:terminal-pairing-integral}.
  3676	
  3677	  Symmetrizing a chain measure does not change its stochastic integral: the
  3678	  product of its $n$ scalar field values is invariant under relabeling. Thus,
  3679	  averaging the $n!$ pushforwards of $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$ with coefficient
  3680	  $1/n!$ gives the same $Y_n$. There is no additional $n!$ factor
  3681	  in~\eqref{E:terminal-wick-formula}, or $m!n!$ in a two-chain product. This
  3682	  identifies the ordinary ordered regularized integrals and their symmetrized
  3683	  convention in~\eqref{E:expansion}.
  3684	
  3685	  In dimension three one may first replace $G$ by $p_\eta*G$. Those positive
  3686	  measures have the same masses and converge weakly to $G$. Off the finitely
  3687	  many time cut points, all finite Gaussian moments are bounded continuous
  3688	  functions of the spatial variables. Dominated convergence for their finite
  3689	  Wick sums proves the same limit for the mixed second moments with two Green
  3690	  widths. It gives $L^2$ convergence to the Bochner integral above, exactly the
  3691	  fixed-noise Green convention used in the source.
  3692	
  3693	  If $\mathcal{K} \ge 0$, positivity of the Green measures makes each covariance
  3694	  product nonnegative. Comparing them proves the stated finite-moment
  3695	  monotonicity, including self-pairs and unequal chains. Finally, the ratio of
  3696	  successive right sides of~\eqref{E:terminal-term-majorant}, with an additional
  3697	  factor $|r|^n$, is $|r|\sqrt V T^2/((2n+2)\sqrt{2n+1})$, which tends to zero.
  3698	  The zero-variance case is immediate. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:terminal-wick}.
  3699	\end{proof}

   267	/-- The symplectic form `ω((u,v),(f,g)) = P(u,g) - P(f,v)` for a pairing
   268	`P : U × V → ℝ` (TeX line 36, with `P` the `H^{1/2}`-`H^{-1/2}` duality). -/

   360	    {A : ι → E →L[ℝ] E} {B : E →L[ℝ] E} (hlim : Tendsto A l (𝓝 B))
   361	    (hA : ∀ᶠ i in l, IsCompactOperator (A i)) : IsCompactOperator B :=
   362	  isClosed_setOfPred_isCompactOperator.mem_of_tendsto hlim hA
   363	
   364	/-- The left Young sum `∑_{j<n} (X(p_{j+1}) - X(p_j)) U(p_j, s)` (TeX lines 95-97). -/
   365	def youngSum (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (U : ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (s : ℝ) (p : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :

   370	(TeX lines 94-98). -/
   371	theorem isCompactOperator_youngSum (X : ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (U : ℝ → ℝ → E →L[ℝ] E) (s : ℝ)
   372	    (p : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hX : ∀ j ≤ n, IsCompactOperator (X (p j))) :
   373	    IsCompactOperator (youngSum X U s p n) := by
   374	  unfold youngSum
   375	  refine Finset.sum_induction _ (fun A : E →L[ℝ] E => IsCompactOperator A)

   377	  intro j hj

   382	/-- The ordered product `P_N ⋯ P_0`. -/
   383	def orderedProd (P : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] E) : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] E
   384	  | 0 => P 0
   385	  | n + 1 => P (n + 1) * orderedProd P n

   387	/-- Telescoping (TeX lines 125-128): if every `P_j - Q_j`, `j ≤ N`, is compact, then
   388	`P_N ⋯ P_0 - Q_N ⋯ Q_0` is compact. -/
   389	theorem isCompactOperator_orderedProd_sub (P Q : ℕ → E →L[ℝ] E) (N : ℕ)
   390	    (h : ∀ j ≤ N, IsCompactOperator (P j - Q j)) :
   391	    IsCompactOperator (orderedProd P N - orderedProd Q N) := by
   392	  induction N with
   393	  | zero => simpa [orderedProd] using h 0 le_rfl
   394	  | succ n ih =>
   395	    have hdecomp : orderedProd P (n + 1) - orderedProd Q (n + 1)
   396	        = (P (n + 1) - Q (n + 1)) * orderedProd P n
   397	          + Q (n + 1) * (orderedProd P n - orderedProd Q n) := by
   398	      simp only [orderedProd, sub_mul, mul_sub]
   399	      abel
   400	    rw [hdecomp]
   401	    exact isCompactOperator_add'
   402	      (isCompactOperator_mul_right (h (n + 1) le_rfl) _)
   403	      (isCompactOperator_mul_left _ (ih fun j hj => h j (by omega)))
   404

  5912	
  5913	Formalizes `L:terminal-wick` (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  5914	at `a284420`; the chain measure `E:terminal-chain-measure`, lines 3585-3598; the
  5915	statement, lines 3600-3645, with the displays `E:terminal-term-majorant`
  5916	(3611-3615), `E:terminal-wick-formula` (3619-3622) and
  5917	`E:terminal-pairing-integral` (3624-3637); the proof, lines 3647-3699), built on
  5918	`FiniteWick`, with every stated conclusion proved for real `r` and two inputs
  5919	left outside Lean, and one added hypothesis (3). (1) Supplied: `hmeas`, the a.e. strong measurability of
  5920	`z -> prod_j W(z_j)` as an `L^2(Omega)`-valued map for each `nu n`. In the TeX it
  5921	follows from the cell-wise mean-square continuity ("the product is strongly
  5922	measurable in `L^2` on the stated pieces", lines 3657-3659); it is assumed here,
  5923	almost everywhere only, so it is no stronger than the TeX's claim. (2) Not
  5924	constructed: the chain measures `g_n^{T,x}`. The general theorems take
  5925	arbitrary finite measures `nu n` on `n`-tuples of points; the wrappers take
  5926	finite measures on `n`-tuples of points of `[0,T] x R^d` (`Pt d T`) with total
  5927	mass `chainMass d n T`. `chainMass d n T` is the lower integral of
  5928	`chainWeight d n T`, the recursion on the last vertex of
  5929	`1_{[0,T]^n_<}(s) prod_j G_{s_{j+1}-s_j}(R^d)` with `s_{n+1} = T` and the wave
  5930	Green measures `WaveGreen.waveGreen d` (in `d = 3` the module's documented
  5931	choice of surface measure). Lean proves `chainMass d n T = T^(2n)/(2n)!` for
